coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 6 units (domain root + 15.01, 15.02, 15.05, 15.06, 15.07) and 36 files — matches the expected 6/36 exactly. Every file was read in full through the 3a→3b→3c cycle. Applicable rubric dimensions per file were 1 (Problem Clarity), 3 (Feature Completeness), 7 (Open Question Resolution) and 8 (Structural Compliance); dimensions 2, 4, 5 and 6 were marked N/A across all units because personas, constraints, success metrics and competitive landscape are owned by meta/ files that are outside this domain's scope and are referenced, never redefined, here (see the domain index Role Matrix legend: "Persona definitions live in meta/personas.md — referenced, never redefined here"). applicableCheckpoints per unit = files × 4. Devil's-advocate pass dropped ~14 raw candidates, chiefly: (a) every [PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening] marker in 15.05 (files are still [SURFACE], so the stage genuinely has not run for them — a live deferral, not a spent one); (b) 15.01/15.02 sub-domain CX PENDING markers, all of which are answered by a cross-reference in a leaf file (handshake timeout → 15.01.03 Q-01; fork ownership → 15.01.06 Q-01; mid-checkout race → 15.02.02 edge rows; payout-vs-flag → 15.02.01 Q-03); (c) the ambiguous bare "(D-01)" citation in 15.02.02 (its DT-01 disambiguates it as the parent index's D-01); (d) 15.05.02's seller-commissioned-appraisal row (defused by D-02, appraisals have no public form); (e) unquantified recompute cadence in 15.05.01 (downstream layer). No blocking findings survived: nothing in this domain leaves an implementer unable to proceed without inventing product behaviour outright.

findings.claim: The domain index's own summary of the tree contradicts the tree in three independent places: the cross-cut counts, the leaf-feature count, and the Status column of the Children table (plus the prose note under it).
findings.evidence: gear-registry-ownership-index.md:48 — "**Cross-cuts**: [gear-registry-ownership-cx.md](./gear-registry-ownership-cx.md) — 10 confirmed pairs, 5 rejected, 5 mechanisms escalated to the platform level." but gear-registry-ownership-cx.md:5 — "**Status**: [DEEP] — 10 children; 19 intra-domain cross-cuts synthesised, 6 pairs rejected, 5 mechanisms escalated to the platform level." and the CX file actually carries CX-01…CX-19 (lines 26–44) and R-01…R-06 (lines 497–502). gear-registry-ownership-index.md:29 — "21 leaf features total. All `[SURFACE]` pending Step 5 deepening." but the tree holds 24 leaf features (6+4+3+3+3 inside the five sub-domains, plus 15.03/15.04/15.08/15.09/15.10), which is exactly the number the same file's own MoSCoW table enumerates at lines 105–107 (1 Must + 10 Should + 13 Could = 24). Children table Status column (lines 33–42) lists all five sub-domains as `[BREADTH]` and all five leaf features as `[SURFACE]`, while on disk 15.05/15.06/15.07 indexes are `[SURFACE]` and 15.04/15.08/15.09 are `[PARTIAL]`; the prose at line 29 ("All `[SURFACE]`") also contradicts the `[BREADTH]` values in its own table.
findings.forcedInvention: A downstream reader deciding whether a node still needs deepening must pick between the index's Status column, the index's prose, and the file's own front-matter — three different answers for 15.04, 15.05, 15.06, 15.07, 15.08 and 15.09.

findings.claim: The domain CX file was renumbered after its consumers were written, and the anchors pointing into it were not updated — at least ten `#CX-NN` references across five units now resolve to an unrelated cross-cut. The CX file itself admits the renumbering in passing.
findings.evidence: gear-registry-ownership-cx.md:161 — "A new link does **not** trigger revaluation (see CX-08 in the old numbering / the deliberate half-connection to valuation)." Consequent stale anchors: 15.03-service-repair-modification-history.md:56 — "Routed to 15.05.01; see `#CX-04`" and :82 — "Triggers revaluation in **15.05.01 Automated Valuation** … see `#CX-04`", but domain CX-04 is "Identity & Provenance ↔ Custody" (cx:29) and the service→valuation pair is CX-10 (cx:35). 15.04-gear-collection-visibility.md:86 — "see [gear-registry-ownership-cx.md](./gear-registry-ownership-cx.md)`#CX-07`, the domain's most important cross-cut", but the exposure hazard is CX-06 (cx:31 and cx:168 "### CX-06: … (THE EXPOSURE HAZARD)") while CX-07 is "Stolen Registry ↔ Valuation & Insurance" (cx:199). Same error at gear-registry-ownership-index.md:128 ("a targeting package for endemic gear theft (CX-07)"), 15.01.01-gear-record-serial-identity.md:162 and :191, and 15.07.03-backline-list-publication.md:103. 15.08-custody-loans-consignment.md:93 cites `#CX-05` for theft-report standing (actual: CX-08) and :94 cites `#CX-06` for rig/asset-register dependence (actual: CX-15/CX-18). 15.06.02-compatibility-oracle.md:83, 15.07.03:98 and 15.07-studio-backline-asset-register-cx.md:122 cite `#CX-10` for oracle↔published-backline (actual: CX-17). 15.06.01:81 and 15.10:81 cite `#CX-09` for rig↔case many-to-many (actual: CX-16).
findings.forcedInvention: A spec writer following any of these anchors lands on a different relationship than the sentence promises — e.g. following 15.03's revaluation pointer yields the custody cross-cut.

findings.claim: 15.08 Q-01 is marked RESOLVED but its final sentence opens a residual product decision — who has standing to file a theft report when the custody record is `stale` or `disputed` — that carries no owner, no deferral target, and no row of its own anywhere in the tree.
findings.evidence: 15.08-custody-loans-consignment.md:114 — "| Q-01 | ~~Who has standing to report gear stolen when custody and ownership differ…~~ **RESOLVED (D-64 / DQ-MG-04, ratified 2026-07-21)** — **both**, bounded: *\"The owner or a party in a `15.08` custody state may file, with capacity recorded…\"* … **Standing under `stale` and `disputed` custody remains open.** | User | ✅ …". The same residual is echoed at 15.02.01-theft-report-serial-flagging.md:60 ("Standing under `stale` and `disputed` custody is still open") also inside a closed row. Neither file opens a tracked question for it, and the six enumerated custody reasons (15.08:32–37: Loan · Service · Consignment · Hire · In transit · Room-resident) are orthogonal to the `stale`/`disputed` lifecycle states (15.08:75–76), so the ratified rule does not decide the case.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a holder whose custody record is disputed (i.e. the owner says the gear was returned) may light a theft flag on it — the exact abuse case — must be invented by the implementer.

findings.claim: 15.09 specifies behaviour for a deleted/deregistered gear record and points at "15.01 deletion rules" and "15.01.03 deletion/deregistration rules", but 15.01.01 D-10 states that gear records have no terminal state and that deletion is not offered, and 15.01.03 (the transfer handshake) contains no deletion rules at all.
findings.evidence: 15.09-gear-discography.md:73 — "| Gear record deleted/deregistered while it carries a discography | The session facts live in domain 02, not on the gear record; deletion cannot erase a credit. The gear identity is tombstoned, not vaporised | The credit still names the object; the object's own passport is gone or archived per 15.01 deletion rules |" and :102 — "and on **15.01.03 deletion/deregistration rules** for the tombstone case in the edge table". Against 15.01.01-gear-record-serial-identity.md:221 — "| D-10 | **The record has no terminal state.** \"Destroyed\" is an appended, reversible fact; deletion is not offered |" and :118 — "Deletion is not offered; erasure obligations are Q-04's problem, not a product affordance." 15.01.03-ownership-transfer-handshake.md carries only D-01 and D-02 (lines 93–94), neither about deletion.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a tombstoned/archived gear-record state exists at all, and what "the object's own passport is gone" renders as, when the owning feature forbids deletion outright.

findings.claim: 15.01.05 D-03 declares that this file authors the canonical identity-confidence value set and that 15.01.01 "never defines its own" — but 15.01.05 contains no value list anywhere, while 15.01.01 does define the six values and simultaneously declares them provisional and pending a synthesis pass against 15.01.05's.
findings.evidence: 15.01.05-non-serialized-contested-identity.md:93 — "| D-03 | **DQ-MG-05:** this file **authors** the canonical identity-confidence value set; `15.01.01` renders it and never defines its own | … The values are the six already in use on disk; relocating them costs nothing because no downstream literal binds to them today." No enumeration of those six values appears anywhere in 15.01.05. The only enumeration on disk is 15.01.01-gear-record-serial-identity.md:87–94 (`serial-confirmed` · `serial-typed` · `serial-reconstructed` · `photo-bound (no serial)` · `era-unknown` · `numbers-disagree`), immediately followed at :96–98 by "15.01.05 owns resolution logic and the authoritative value set; this feature owns the render and the record's behaviour at each level. The vocabulary above is proposed from the render side and is flagged for Step 6 synthesis against 15.01.05's."
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the six values are ratified (per 15.01.05 D-03) or a render-side proposal awaiting reconciliation (per 15.01.01) — and, if the latter, what 15.01.05's competing set is, since none exists.

findings.claim: When an attester's account is banned or deleted, 15.01.04 says the affected link's attestation strength "drops" — but it names no target level, and 15.01.02's ratified tier rule recomputes only on withdrawn evidence, which a banned attester's still-standing confirmation is not. 15.01.04 also disclaims owning any fact, so no feature owns the reduced value.
findings.evidence: 15.01.04-provenance-chain-view.md:57 — "| An event's attester was later banned or deleted their account (15.01.02) | The event survives … but its attestation strength drops to reflect that the witness can no longer be reached to re-confirm | \"Service attested in 2022 by an account no longer active\" — event kept, confidence for that link reduced, never silently removed |". Against 15.01.02-ownership-claim-verification.md:112 — "| D-03 | The tier is the maximum of standing confirmed evidence, recomputable downward | … withdrawn evidence recomputes the tier down to what remains (DT-04). \"Confirmed\" means \"confirmed and not withdrawn\"." — a ban is neither a recant nor a retraction. And 15.01.04:91 — "| D-01 | The chain is a view, not a store | Every fact it shows is owned by the feature that produced it."
findings.forcedInvention: How far the strength drops (Counter-attested → Asserted? a sub-tier?), and whether the drop is a render-only caveat on the chain or an actual recomputation of the 15.01.02 claim tier a buyer reads at point of sale.

findings.claim: Standing to file a theft report is stated as deferred in 15.02.01's edge table and as unresolved in the domain CX, while 15.02.01's own Q-01 and 15.08's Q-01 both record it as ratified on 2026-07-21; the resolving row also cites a "D-05" that does not exist in 15.02.01's Decisions table.
findings.evidence: 15.02.01-theft-report-serial-flagging.md:51 — "| Stolen gear was under someone else's custody (15.08) | Both the owner and the holder may file … | … Final standing rules deferred — see Q-01 and 15.08 Q-01. |" against the same file's :99 — "| Q-01 | ~~Who has standing to file when ownership and custody differ?~~ **Resolved by DQ-MG-04 / D-05 (2026-07-21):** the owner **or** a party in a custody state `15.08` already enumerates may file, with filing capacity recorded on the flag. … | Owner | ✅ `/ideate-validate`, 2026-07-21 |" — but that file's Decisions table holds only D-01 and D-02 (:92–93). The domain CX still carries the stale state at gear-registry-ownership-cx.md:239 — "3. **Permission intersection**: Who has standing to file? Unresolved — 15.08 Q-01.", and :228 — "When owner and holder differ, both may file, but standing rules are unresolved (Q-04)." 15.08-custody-loans-consignment.md:114 records the same question as "**RESOLVED (D-64 / DQ-MG-04, ratified 2026-07-21)**".
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer reading the edge row alone treats filing standing as unspecified and invents it; one reading Q-01 implements the enumerated-custody-state rule with capacity recorded on the flag.

findings.claim: The flag state table answers "Blocks sale?" concretely for five of six states but gives `resolved` the answer "Per outcome" — and no outcome vocabulary is defined in this file, in 15.02.02, or anywhere else in the domain.
findings.evidence: 15.02.04-false-flag-dispute-lifecycle.md:43 — "| `resolved` | Dispute reached a terminal external outcome (terminal) | Per outcome | outcome recorded, not adjudicated by platform |", reached per :53–54 ("→ `resolved` (external authority settles and a party reports it, or the matter is routed to domain 24 and closed there)") and per :92 ("| Both parties have genuine claims (band split, gear bought jointly) | … | Flag → `resolved` (routed out) …"). 15.02.02-point-of-sale-serial-screening.md enumerates screening renders for hit, contested, retro-screen, unreachable-store, serial-less and mid-checkout cases (:50–57) but never for `resolved`. The file's Q-01 (:145) treats the six-value state set as locked and defers only "binding those states, their transitions and their guard conditions into a contract" to `/write-be-spec`.
findings.forcedInvention: The set of terminal external outcomes and which of them block a listing — i.e. whether a flag routed out to domain 24 as an ownership dispute leaves the gear sellable on WeJammin or not.

findings.claim: 15.06.03 defers the disclosure of held-not-owned gear on an outgoing spec sheet to `/ideate-discover` Step 5 deepening, while the same file's open-question rows state that stage is completed; the domain CX independently records the question as unresolved, and no tracked question in the unit carries it.
findings.evidence: 15.06.03-rig-spec-sheet-source-data.md:54 — "| Rig contains gear the user doesn't own (15.08) | The sheet discloses someone else's asset | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` |", against the same file's Q-01 (:97), Q-02 (:98) and Q-03 (:99), each ending "Deferral re-pointed from the completed `/ideate-discover` Step 5." None of those three rows covers this case (they cover live-read-vs-snapshot, stage-plot scope, and serial stripping). The domain CX confirms it is genuinely open: gear-registry-ownership-cx.md:395 — "3. **Permission intersection**: Exporting a rig spec (15.06.03) that includes held-not-owned gear discloses someone else's asset — real and unresolved (CX-18 sibling)."
findings.forcedInvention: Whether an exported sheet lists borrowed/house/consigned gear at all, and whether the owner's consent is required before their asset appears on a document sent to a third-party venue.

findings.claim: The advance-vs-show staleness case — a band advances against a published backline list that changes before the date — is deferred in two 15.07 files to `/ideate-discover` Step 5 deepening, a stage those same files' question rows describe as completed, and no open question in the unit carries it.
findings.evidence: 15.07.03-backline-list-publication.md:74 — "| Band advanced against a list that changed after | Both parties' documents were true when exchanged | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — mirrors 15.06.03 DT-03 exactly, pointing the other way |" and 15.07.02-asset-condition-availability-state.md:65 — "| Asset breaks between advance and show | Both parties' documents were correct when exchanged | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — mirrors 15.06.03 DT-03 |". Both files re-point their real questions off that stage: 15.07.03 Q-02 and Q-03 (:120, :121) and 15.07.02 Q-02 (:113) each close with "Deferral re-pointed from the completed `/ideate-discover` Step 5." 15.07.03 Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 cover condition suppression, on-loan publishability and photo serials — none covers advance-vs-show drift; the domain CX only describes it (gear-registry-ownership-cx.md:444 — "The check is a snapshot; the show is weeks later. Both the room's list and the band's sheet were true when exchanged and can both be wrong by the date.").
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a material change to a published register re-notifies parties who already advanced against it, and what the room owes a band that planned around an asset that has since failed.
